translations.literal: In each case set the general-use fraction, multiply by mean departure, divide by that day's departure interval—this is the fixed-use fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Set each general-use fraction, multiply by mean departure, divide by the day's departure interval to obtain the fixed-use fraction.

translations.literal: Use it to subtract from the new-or-full-moon fixed fraction—this is the beginning of wane.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract it from the syzygy fixed fraction to obtain first contact.

translations.literal: Add it—this is the end of recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Add it to obtain last contact.

sentences.zh: 加時常分，如食甚術推之，得虧初、復末定分。

translations.literal: Added-time constant fraction: project as in the greatest-eclipse technique to obtain the fixed fractions for beginning of wane and end of recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the added-time constant fraction by the greatest-eclipse procedure to obtain fixed times for first and last contact.

sentences.zh: 置初、甚、末定分，各以辰則除之，為辰；

translations.literal: Set the beginning, greatest, and end fixed fractions; in each case divide by the double-hour rule—this is the double-hour;
translations.idiomatic: Set the first-contact, greatest, and last-contact fixed fractions; divide each by the double-hour divisor to obtain the double-hour;

sentences.zh: 經法除之，為刻：即初、甚、末之辰刻也。

translations.literal: divide by the canonical method—this is the quarter: these are the double-hours and quarters of beginning, greatest, and end.
translations.idiomatic: divide the remainder by the canonical method for quarters—the double-hours and quarters of first contact, maximum, and last contact.

translations.literal: Where waning eclipse arises
translations.idiomatic: Direction of eclipse onset

sentences.zh: 日食起虧自西，月食起虧自東。

translations.literal: Solar eclipses begin waning from the west; lunar eclipses begin waning from the east.
translations.idiomatic: Solar eclipses first contact in the west; lunar eclipses first contact in the east.

sentences.zh: 其食分少者，月行陽道，則日食偏南，月食偏北；

translations.literal: When the eclipse fraction is small, if the moon travels the yang path, then the solar eclipse is biased south and the lunar eclipse biased north;
translations.idiomatic: For small magnitude, when the Moon is on the yang path, solar eclipses skew south and lunar eclipses north;

sentences.zh: 陰道，則日食偏北，月食偏南：此常數也。

translations.literal: on the yin path, then the solar eclipse is biased north and the lunar eclipse biased south: these are the constant numbers.
translations.idiomatic: on the yin path, solar eclipses skew north and lunar south—these are the standard constants.

sentences.zh: 立春後，立夏前，食分多，則日食偏南，月食偏北；

translations.literal: After Establishment of Spring and before Establishment of Summer, when the eclipse fraction is large, then the solar eclipse is biased south and the lunar eclipse biased north;
translations.idiomatic: From after Lichun to before Lixia, large eclipses bias solar south and lunar north;

sentences.zh: 立秋後，立冬前，食分多，則日食偏北，月食偏南：此黃道斜正也。

translations.literal: after Establishment of Autumn and before Establishment of Winter, when the eclipse fraction is large, then the solar eclipse is biased north and the lunar eclipse biased south: this is Yellow Path oblique-and-direct.
translations.idiomatic: from after Liqiu to before Lidong, large eclipses bias solar north and lunar south—this follows ecliptic obliquity.

sentences.zh: 陽道交前，陰道交後，食分多，則日食偏南，月食偏北；

translations.literal: Yang path before crossing, yin path after crossing—when the eclipse fraction is large, then the solar eclipse is biased south and the lunar eclipse biased north;
translations.idiomatic: Yang path before the node and yin path after it, large eclipses bias solar south and lunar north;

sentences.zh: 陽道交後，陰道交前，食分多，則日食偏北，月食偏南：此九道斜正也。

translations.literal: yang path after crossing, yin path before crossing—when the eclipse fraction is large, then the solar eclipse is biased north and the lunar eclipse biased south: this is nine-path oblique-and-direct.
translations.idiomatic: yang path after the node and yin path before it, large eclipses bias solar north and lunar south—this follows lunar-path obliquity.

sentences.zh: 黃道比常數所偏差少，九道比黃道所偏又四分之一：皆據午而言之。

translations.literal: The Yellow Path's deviation from the constant numbers is less; the nine paths' deviation from the Yellow Path is again one-fourth: all are spoken with reference to noon.
translations.idiomatic: Ecliptic deviation from the standard constants is smaller; lunar-path deviation from the ecliptic is a further quarter—all reckoned from local noon.

sentences.zh: 若午前午後，一理偏南，一理偏北，及消息所食分數多少，以定初、甚、末之方，即各得所求也。

translations.literal: If before or after noon, one principle biases south and one biases north, and according to the waxing-and-waning how great or small the eclipse fraction is, use these to fix the directions of beginning, greatest, and end—then each sought result is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: For morning or afternoon, one rule skews south and one north; combine eclipse magnitude with seasonal phase to fix the azimuths of first contact, maximum, and last contact—each desired result then follows.

translations.literal: Eclipse accompanying exit-and-entry fraction
translations.idiomatic: Fraction for eclipses at sunrise or sunset

sentences.zh: 視其日出入分，在虧初定分已上，復末定分已下，即帶食出入。

translations.literal: Observe that day's exit-and-entry fraction: if it is above the beginning-of-wane fixed fraction and below the end-of-recovery fixed fraction, then the eclipse accompanies exit or entry.
translations.idiomatic: If the day's sunrise/sunset fraction falls between the first-contact and last-contact fixed fractions, the eclipse occurs at rising or setting.

sentences.zh: 食甚在出入分已下者，以出入分減復末定分，為帶食差。

translations.literal: If greatest eclipse is below the exit-and-entry fraction, subtract the exit-and-entry fraction from the end-of-recovery fixed fraction—this is the accompanying-eclipse difference.
translations.idiomatic: If greatest eclipse precedes sunrise/sunset, subtract the exit-and-entry fraction from the last-contact fixed fraction for the horizon correction.

sentences.zh: 食甚在出入分已上者，以虧初定分減出入分，為帶食差。

translations.literal: If greatest eclipse is above the exit-and-entry fraction, subtract the exit-and-entry fraction from the beginning-of-wane fixed fraction—this is the accompanying-eclipse difference.
translations.idiomatic: If greatest eclipse follows sunrise/sunset, subtract the exit-and-entry fraction from the first-contact fixed fraction for the horizon correction.

sentences.zh: 各置帶食差，以距食分乘之，定用分而一，日以四百七十八、月以五百二十六除，為帶食之大分；

translations.literal: ◎ mid-day mid-star
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Mean conjunction: day and central star

sentences.zh: 置氣積，以其星周率除之，為周數；

translations.literal: Set the qi accumulation, divide it by that star's cycle rate, to obtain cycle count;
translations.idiomatic: Set the qi accumulation and divide by the planet's cycle rate to obtain the number of complete cycles;

sentences.zh: 不盡為天正中氣積前合。

translations.literal: what does not exhaust is heaven's central qi accumulation prior conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder is the accumulation before conjunction at celestial mid-qi.

sentences.zh: 用減歲率，為前年天正中氣後合。

translations.literal: Use it to subtract from the year rate, for the prior year's heaven's central qi posterior conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract it from the annual rate to obtain the post-conjunction at celestial mid-qi in the preceding year.

sentences.zh: 如不足減，則加歲率以減之，為次前年天正中氣後合。

translations.literal: If insufficient to subtract, then add the year rate to subtract it, for the next prior year's heaven's central qi posterior conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: If the subtraction cannot be completed, add one annual rate and subtract again to obtain the post-conjunction two years earlier.

sentences.zh: 各以統法約之，為日、為度，即所求平合中日、中星也。

translations.literal: Each reduce by the unification method, as days, as degrees—this is the sought mean-conjunction mid-day and mid-star.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce each by the unification divisor to obtain days and degrees—the mean-conjunction mid-day and central star sought.

sentences.zh: 置中日，以逐段變日累加之，即逐段中日也。

translations.literal: Set the mid-day, with each segment's mutation days accumulate and add—this is each segment's mid-day.
translations.idiomatic: Set the mid-day and add the segment mutation-days cumulatively to obtain each segment's mid-day.

sentences.zh: 置中星，以逐段變度順加、退減之，即得逐段中星。

translations.literal: Set the mid-star, with each segment's mutation degrees prograde add and retrograde subtract—thus obtain each segment's mid-star.
translations.idiomatic: Set the central star and apply each segment's mutation-degrees, adding in direct motion and subtracting in retrograde, to obtain each segment's central star.

sentences.zh: 金水夕伏晨見，皆退變也。

translations.literal: Metal and Water evening hiding morning appearance—all are retrograde mutations.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mercury evening concealment and morning appearance all use retrograde mutation.

translations.literal: Set the mutation rate.
translations.idiomatic: Set the variation rate.

sentences.zh: 以周數乘之，以曆率去之，余滿統法為度。

translations.literal: Multiply by cycle count, remove the calendar rate, remainder filling the unification method is degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the cycle count, remove multiples of the calendar rate, and convert the remainder to degrees by the unification divisor.

translations.literal: Below mid-cycle, is prior;
translations.idiomatic: If below mid-cycle, it is prior;

sentences.zh: 以上，減去歷中，為後：即所求平合入歷。

translations.literal: Above, subtract mid-cycle, is posterior: this is the sought mean-conjunction entry into the cycle.
translations.idiomatic: if above, subtract the mid-cycle value to obtain the posterior portion—the mean-conjunction's entry into the epicycle sought.

sentences.zh: 以逐段變曆累加之，得逐段入歷也。

translations.literal: With each segment's mutation calendar accumulate and add, obtain each segment's entry into the cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Add the segment mutation-calendar values cumulatively to obtain each segment's epicycle entry.

translations.literal: latter-latter fixed numbers
translations.idiomatic: Prior-posterior fixed corrections

sentences.zh: 置入歷分，以其度損益率乘之，經法而一，用損益其下先後數，即所求也。

translations.literal: Set the entry-into-cycle parts, multiply by its degree's decrease-increase rate, canonical method and one, use to decrease-increase the prior-posterior numbers below—this is what is sought.
translations.idiomatic: Set the epicycle parts, multiply by the degree's variation rate, divide by the canonical divisor, and apply the result to adjust the prior-posterior constants below—the value sought.

translations.literal: ◎ regular day fixed star
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Mean day and corrected star

sentences.zh: 置中日中星，各以先後定數，先加、後減之，留用前段先後數，太白順伏見及前順疾次疾後次遲次疾、辰星順伏見及前疾後遲，並先減、後加之，即各為其段常日定星。

translations.literal: Set mid-day mid-star, each with prior-posterior fixed numbers, prior add and posterior subtract; at station use the prior segment's prior-posterior numbers—Great White prograde hiding appearance and prior prograde-rapid secondary-rapid posterior secondary-slow secondary-rapid, Hour Star prograde hiding appearance and prior rapid posterior slow, all prior subtract and posterior add—thus each becomes that segment's regular day fixed star.
translations.idiomatic: Set the mean day and central star and apply the prior-posterior corrections, adding when prior and subtracting when posterior; at stations use the prior segment's values. For Venus in direct concealment/appearance and the segments prior swift, secondary swift, posterior secondary slow, and secondary swift, and for Mercury in direct concealment/appearance with prior swift and posterior slow, reverse the rule (subtract when prior, add when posterior) to obtain each segment's mean day and corrected star.

sentences.zh: 置定星，以其年天正中氣日躔黃道宿次加而命之，得逐段末日加時宿度也。

translations.literal: Set the fixed star, with that year's heaven's central qi day progression Yellow Path lodge sequence add and name it, obtain each segment's last-day added-time lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Set the corrected star, add the year's celestial mid-qi solar longitude on the ecliptic and name the lodge, to obtain each segment's terminal-day added-time lodge position.

translations.literal: expansion-contraction fixed numbers
translations.idiomatic: Expansion and contraction corrections

sentences.zh: 置常日，如歲中以下，為在盈；

translations.literal: Set the regular day, if like year-mid or below, is located in expansion;
translations.idiomatic: Set the mean day; if it does not exceed the annual mid-cycle, it lies in the expansion phase;

sentences.zh: 以上，減去歲中，余為在縮：即常日入盈縮歷也。

translations.literal: above, subtract year-mid, remainder is located in contraction: this is the regular day's entry into expansion-contraction cycle.
translations.idiomatic: if above, subtract the annual mid-cycle; the remainder lies in contraction—the mean day's entry into the expansion-contraction epicycle.

translations.literal: Set the cycle parts.
translations.idiomatic: Set the epicycle parts.

sentences.zh: 以其日損益率乘之，經法而一，用損益其下盈縮數，即得所求也。

translations.literal: Multiply by that day's decrease-increase rate, canonical method and one, use to decrease-increase the expansion-contraction numbers below—thus obtain what is sought.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the day's variation rate, divide by the canonical divisor, and adjust the expansion-contraction constant below to obtain the value sought.

sentences.zh: 置常日，以盈縮定數盈減、縮加之，為定日。

translations.literal: Set the regular day, with expansion-contraction fixed numbers expansion subtract and contraction add, for fixed day.
translations.idiomatic: Set the mean day and subtract in expansion or add in contraction according to the correction to obtain the corrected day.

sentences.zh: 以其年天正中氣加而命之，即逐段末日加時日辰也。

translations.literal: With that year's heaven's central qi add and name it—this is each segment's last-day added-time day and double-hour.
translations.idiomatic: Add the year's celestial mid-qi and name the result to obtain each segment's terminal-day added-time date and hour.

translations.literal: ◎ entry into mid qi and nodes
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Entry into qi and solar terms

sentences.zh: 置定日，以氣策除之，命起冬至，即所入氣日數也。

translations.literal: Set the fixed day, divide by the qi tally, name from Winter Solstice—this is the qi day-count entered.
translations.idiomatic: Set the corrected day, divide by the qi divisor, and count from the winter solstice to obtain the qi and day entered.

translations.literal: ◎ level motion parts
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Mean daily motion

sentences.zh: 置定日，以前段定日減之，為日率；

translations.literal: Set the fixed day, subtract the prior segment's fixed day, for day rate;
translations.idiomatic: Set the corrected day and subtract the prior segment's corrected day to obtain the day rate;

sentences.zh: 定星與前段定星相減，為度率。

translations.literal: fixed star with prior segment's fixed star mutually subtract, for degree rate.
translations.idiomatic: subtract the prior segment's corrected star from the current corrected star to obtain the degree rate.

sentences.zh: 通度率，以經法乘之，通日率而一，為平行分。

translations.literal: Communicate the degree rate, multiply by canonical method, communicate day rate and one, for level motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: Convert the degree rate, multiply by the canonical divisor, divide by the converted day rate, to obtain the mean daily motion.

translations.literal: ◎ initial-final motion parts
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Initial and final daily motion

sentences.zh: 近伏段與伏段平行分，合而半之，為其段近伏行分。

translations.literal: Near-hiding segment with hiding segment level motion parts, combine and halve, for that segment's near-hiding motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: For a segment near concealment, average its mean motion with that of the concealment segment to obtain the near-concealment daily motion.

sentences.zh: 以平行分減之，余減平行分，為其段遠伏行分。

translations.literal: Subtract level motion parts from it, remainder subtracts level motion parts, for that segment's far-hiding motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract from the mean motion; subtract the remainder again from the mean motion to obtain the far-concealment daily motion.

translations.literal: Near-station segment near-station motion parts void.
translations.idiomatic: Near-station segment: near-station daily motion is blank.

sentences.zh: 倍平行分為其段遠留行分。

translations.literal: Double the level motion parts for that segment's far-station motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: Double the mean daily motion to obtain the far-station daily motion.

sentences.zh: 其不近伏留段，皆以順行二段平行分，合而半之，為前段末日、後段初日行分。

translations.literal: Those not near hiding or station segments—all take two prograde segments' level motion parts, combine and halve, for prior segment's last day and posterior segment's first day motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: For segments not near concealment or station, average the mean motions of the two adjacent direct-motion segments to obtain the last day of the prior segment and the first day of the next.

sentences.zh: 各與其段平行分相減，平行分多，則加平行分；

translations.literal: Each with its segment's level motion parts mutually subtract; if level motion parts are many, then add level motion parts;
translations.idiomatic: Compare each with its segment's mean motion; if the mean motion is greater, add the mean motion;

sentences.zh: 平行分少，則減平行分，即前段初日、後段末日行分。

translations.literal: if level motion parts are few, then subtract level motion parts—this is prior segment's first day and posterior segment's last day motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: if less, subtract the mean motion—to obtain the first day of the prior segment and the last day of the posterior segment.

sentences.zh: 其不近伏留段，退行則以遲段近疾行分，為疾段近遲行分，所得與平行分相減，平行分多，則加之，少則減之：皆為遠遲行分也。

translations.literal: Those not near hiding or station segments—in retrograde motion then take the slow segment's near-rapid motion parts as the rapid segment's near-slow motion parts; what is obtained with level motion parts mutually subtract—if level motion parts many then add, if few then subtract: all are far-slow motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: For segments not near concealment or station in retrograde motion, take the slow segment's near-swift motion as the swift segment's near-slow motion; compare with the mean motion and add if the mean is greater or subtract if less—all yielding the far-slow daily motion.

translations.literal: initial motion midnight lodge sequence
translations.idiomatic: Initial motion: midnight lodge position

sentences.zh: 置經法，以前段末日加時分減之：余乘前段末日行分，經法而一；

translations.literal: Set the canonical method, subtract the prior segment's last-day added-time parts: remainder multiply the prior segment's last-day motion parts, canonical method and one;
translations.idiomatic: Set the canonical divisor and subtract the prior segment's terminal-day added-time parts; multiply the remainder by that day's motion and divide by the canonical divisor;

sentences.zh: 用順加、退減前段末日加時宿度，為其段初行昏後夜半宿度也。

translations.literal: use prograde add and retrograde subtract on the prior segment's last-day added-time lodge degrees, for that segment's initial motion dusk-after midnight lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: add in direct motion or subtract in retrograde from the prior segment's terminal-day added-time lodge position to obtain this segment's initial dusk-after-midnight lodge position.

translations.literal: ◎ each-day motion parts
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Daily motion

translations.literal: initial-final motion parts mutually subtract, for difference rate.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the initial from the final daily motion to obtain the difference rate.

sentences.zh: 累計其段初行昏後夜半距後段初行昏後夜半日數除之，為日差。

translations.literal: Accumulate and count from this segment's initial motion dusk-after midnight to the posterior segment's initial motion dusk-after midnight day-count and divide—this is day difference.
translations.idiomatic: Count the days from this segment's initial dusk-after-midnight to the next segment's initial dusk-after-midnight and divide to obtain the daily increment.

sentences.zh: 半日差，以減多、加少為其段初末定行分。

translations.literal: Halve the day difference, use to subtract the greater and add the lesser for that segment's initial-final fixed motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: Halve the daily increment and apply it to reduce the larger and increase the smaller to obtain the segment's corrected initial and final motion.

sentences.zh: 置初定行分，用日差末多則累加、末少則累減，為每日行分。

translations.literal: Set the initial fixed motion parts; if day difference's end is many then accumulate add, if end is few then accumulate subtract—for each-day motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: Set the corrected initial motion and accumulate the daily increment, adding when the final motion is greater and subtracting when less, to obtain each day's motion.

sentences.zh: 以每日行分順加、退減初行昏後夜半宿度，為每日昏後夜半星所至宿度也。

translations.literal: With each-day motion parts prograde add and retrograde subtract from initial motion dusk-after midnight lodge degrees—for each day dusk-after midnight the star's arrived-at lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Apply each day's motion, adding in direct motion and subtracting in retrograde from the initial dusk-after-midnight position, to obtain the star's lodge at dusk after midnight for each day.

translations.literal: first fix day dusk-after midnight lodge sequence
translations.idiomatic: Corrected day: dusk-after-midnight lodge position

sentences.zh: 自初日累計距所求日數，以乘其段日差；

translations.literal: From the initial day accumulate and count the distance to the day sought, multiply by that segment's day difference;
translations.idiomatic: Count the days from the segment's first day to the day sought and multiply by the segment's daily increment;

sentences.zh: 末多用加、末少用減初日行分，為其日行分。

translations.literal: if end many then add, if end few then subtract from initial-day motion parts—for that day's motion parts.
translations.idiomatic: add to or subtract from the first day's motion according to whether the final motion is greater or less to obtain that day's motion.

sentences.zh: 合初日而半之，以所累計日乘之，用順加、退減其段初行昏後夜半宿次，即所求也。

translations.literal: Combine with the initial day and halve, multiply by the accumulated days counted, use prograde add and retrograde subtract on that segment's initial motion dusk-after midnight lodge sequence—this is what is sought.
translations.idiomatic: Average with the first day's motion, multiply by the elapsed days, and add or subtract from the segment's initial dusk-after-midnight lodge position in direct or retrograde motion to obtain the result sought.

translations.idiomatic: Qintian Calendar, procedure for pacing emergence and retraction—hou divisor: 5; remainder 524; fraction 45.

translations.idiomatic: Hexagram divisor: 6; remainder 629; fraction 34.

sentences.zh: 外策：三，三百一十四，六十七。

translations.idiomatic: Outer divisor: 3; remainder 314; fraction 67.

translations.idiomatic: Solar-term surplus: 1,573; fraction 35.

translations.idiomatic: New-moon void: 3,399; fraction 72.

sentences.zh: ◎氣候圖冬至十一月中蚯蚓結麋角解水泉動小寒十二月節雁北鄉鵲始巢雉始雊

translations.literal: ◎ Climate chart: Winter Solstice, eleventh month mid-month—earthworms coil, elk antlers shed, springs stir; Minor Cold, twelfth month first node—geese head north, magpies begin nests, pheasants first crow.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Climate chart — Winter Solstice (11th month, mid-month): earthworms coil; elk shed antlers; springs stir. Minor Cold (12th month, first node): wild geese turn north; magpies begin to nest; pheasants first call.

sentences.zh: 大寒十二月中雞始乳鷙鳥厲疾水澤腹堅立春正月節東風解凍蟄蟲始振魚上冰雨水正月中獺祭魚鴻雁來草木萌動

translations.literal: Major Cold, twelfth month mid-month—hens begin to suckle, fierce birds show sharp flight, marshes' bellies firm; Start of Spring, first month first node—east wind melts ice, hibernating insects first stir, fish ascend to ice; Rain Water, first month mid-month—otters sacrifice fish, wild geese come, plants and trees first sprout.
translations.idiomatic: Major Cold (12th month, mid-month): hens begin brooding; birds of prey grow swift; ice hardens deep in the marshes. Start of Spring (1st month, first node): the east wind thaws the ice; dormant insects stir; fish rise beneath the ice. Rain Water (1st month, mid-month): otters offer fish; wild geese arrive; grass and trees put forth shoots.

sentences.zh: 驚蟄二月節桃始華倉庚鳴鷹化為鳩春分二月中玄鳥至雷乃發聲始電清明三月節桐始華田鼠化為鴽虹始見

translations.literal: Awakening of Insects, second month first node—peaches first flower, orioles cry, hawks transform into turtledoves; Spring Equinox, second month mid-month—dark birds arrive, thunder then sends forth sound, lightning begins; Pure Brightness, third month first node—paulownia first flowers, field mice transform into quails, rainbows first appear.
translations.idiomatic: Awakening of Insects (2nd month, first node): peaches blossom; orioles sing; hawks turn into cuckoos. Spring Equinox (2nd month, mid-month): swallows arrive; thunder sounds; lightning begins. Pure Brightness (3rd month, first node): paulownia blooms; field mice become quails; rainbows first appear.

sentences.zh: 谷雨三月中萍始生鳴鳩拂其羽戴勝降於桑立夏四月節螻蟈鳴蚯蚓出王瓜生小滿四月中苦菜秀靡草死小暑至

translations.literal: Grain Rain, third month mid-month—duckweed first grows, calling doves smooth their feathers, hoopoes descend on mulberry; Start of Summer, fourth month first node—tree crickets cry, earthworms emerge, snake-gourd grows; Minor Fullness, fourth month mid-month—bitter herbs flourish, soft grasses die, minor heat arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain (3rd month, mid-month): duckweed sprouts; turtle-doves preen their feathers; hoopoes alight on mulberry trees. Start of Summer (4th month, first node): tree crickets chirp; earthworms emerge; gourds grow. Minor Fullness (4th month, mid-month): bitter herbs flourish; tender grasses wither; lesser heat draws near.

sentences.zh: 芒種五月節螗螂生鵙始鳴反舌無聲夏至五月中鹿角解蜩始鳴半夏生小暑六月節溫風至蟋蟀居壁鷹乃學習

translations.literal: Grain in Ear, fifth month first node—mantises hatch, shrikes first cry, mockingbirds have no voice; Summer Solstice, fifth month mid-month—deer antlers shed, cicadas first chirp, half-dead grass grows; Minor Heat, sixth month first node—warm winds arrive, crickets dwell in walls, eagles then learn.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in Ear (5th month, first node): praying mantises hatch; shrikes begin to call; mockingbirds fall silent. Summer Solstice (5th month, mid-month): deer shed antlers; cicadas begin to sing; pinellia sprouts. Minor Heat (6th month, first node): warm winds blow; crickets move to the walls; eagles learn to strike.

sentences.zh: 大暑六月中腐草為螢土潤溽暑大雨時行立秋七月節涼風至白露降寒蟬鳴處暑七月中鷹祭鳥天地始肅禾乃登

translations.literal: Major Heat, sixth month mid-month—rotten grass becomes fireflies, earth moist, sweltering heat, great rains fall in season; Start of Autumn, seventh month first node—cool winds arrive, white dew descends, cold cicadas cry; End of Heat, seventh month mid-month—eagles sacrifice birds, heaven and earth first grow austere, grain then ripens.
translations.idiomatic: Major Heat (6th month, mid-month): rotten grass turns to fireflies; the earth grows damp in oppressive heat; heavy rains fall in season. Start of Autumn (7th month, first node): cool winds arrive; white dew descends; cold cicadas cry. End of Heat (7th month, mid-month): eagles offer birds; heaven and earth begin to harden; grain ripens.

sentences.zh: 白露八月節鴻雁來玄鳥歸群鳥養羞秋分八月中雷乃收聲蟄蟲坯戶水始涸寒露九月節鴻雁來賓雀入水為蛤菊有黃華

translations.literal: White Dew, eighth month first node—wild geese come, dark birds return, flocks of birds store delicacies; Autumn Equinox, eighth month mid-month—thunder then gathers sound, hibernating insects seal doorways, water first dries; Cold Dew, ninth month first node—wild geese come as guests, sparrows enter water as clams, chrysanthemums have yellow flowers.
translations.idiomatic: White Dew (8th month, first node): wild geese arrive; swallows return; birds lay up provisions. Autumn Equinox (8th month, mid-month): thunder fades; hibernating creatures block their burrows; waters begin to shrink. Cold Dew (9th month, first node): geese come as guests; sparrows enter the water as clams; chrysanthemums bloom yellow.

translations.literal: Each set at the mid-node—this is the first hou.
translations.idiomatic: Set each at the mid-node of its solar term; that yields the first phenological hou.

sentences.zh: 以候策累加之，即次候也。

translations.literal: With the hou tally accumulate and add—this is the next hou.
translations.idiomatic: Add the hou divisor cumulatively to obtain each successive hou.

translations.literal: ◎ Sixty-four hexagrams.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ The sixty-four hexagrams.

translations.literal: Set at the central qi—this is the duke hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Set at the central qi; that is the duke hexagram.

sentences.zh: 以卦策累加之，即次卦也。

translations.literal: With the hexagram tally accumulate and add—this is the next hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Add the hexagram divisor cumulatively to obtain each successive hexagram.

sentences.zh: 置侯卦，以外策加之，即外卦也。

translations.literal: Set the marquis hexagram; with the outer tally add to it—this is the outer hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: From the marquis hexagram, add the outer divisor to obtain the outer hexagram.

translations.literal: ◎ Five phases in governance.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Governance of the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 置四立之節而命之，即春木、夏火、秋金、冬水用事之初也。

translations.literal: Set the four establishment nodes and name them—this is spring Wood, summer Fire, autumn Metal, winter Water at the beginning of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Fix the four establishment nodes and name them: that marks when Wood governs in spring, Fire in summer, Metal in autumn, and Water in winter.

sentences.zh: 置四季之節，各以維策加之，即土用事也。

translations.literal: Set the four season nodes; to each add the intercalary tally—this is Earth in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Fix the four seasonal nodes and add the intercalary divisor to each; that is when Earth governs.

translations.literal: ◎ Submergence days.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Submergence days (mo days).

sentences.zh: 中節分五千六百二十六秒六十五已上者，用減統法，為有沒分。

translations.literal: Mid-node parts five thousand six hundred twenty-six seconds sixty-five or above—use to subtract the epoch method; this is having submergence parts.
translations.idiomatic: When the mid-node fraction is 5,626 seconds 65 or more, subtract the epoch divisor to obtain the submergence remainder.

sentences.zh: 通氣策以乘之，氣盈而一，滿統法為日；

translations.literal: Communicate the qi tally to multiply it; qi surplus and one, filling the epoch method makes days;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the communicated qi divisor, divide by the qi surplus plus one, and convert remainders filling the epoch divisor into days;

sentences.zh: 用加其氣而命之，即所求沒日也。

translations.literal: Use to add to its qi and name it—this is the sought submergence day.
translations.idiomatic: add the result to the qi and name the day to obtain the submergence day sought.

translations.literal: ◎ Extinction days.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Extinction days (extinguished days).

sentences.zh: 常朔分朔虛已下者，為滅分。

translations.literal: When the regular new-moon parts are at or below the new-moon void—this is extinction parts.
translations.idiomatic: When the regular new-moon fraction falls at or below the new-moon void, that is the extinction remainder.

sentences.zh: 以朔率乘之，朔虛而一，盈統法為日；

translations.literal: With the new-moon rate multiply it; new-moon void and one, filling the epoch method makes days;
translations.idiomatic: multiply by the new-moon rate, divide by the new-moon void plus one, and convert remainders filling the epoch divisor into days;

sentences.zh: 用加其朔而命之，即所求滅日也。

translations.literal: Use to add to its new moon and name it—this is the sought extinction day.
translations.idiomatic: add the result to the new moon and name the day to obtain the extinction day sought.

sentences.zh: 右樸所撰《欽天曆經》四篇。

translations.literal: At right, four chapters composed by Pu: the 《Qintian Calendar Classic》.
translations.idiomatic: Above are the four treatises Wang Pu composed for the 《欽天曆經》 (Classic of the Respectful-of-Heaven Calendar).

sentences.zh: 《舊史》亡其《步發斂》一篇，而在者三篇，簡略不完，不足為法。

translations.literal: The 《Old History》 lost its one chapter 《Pacing Emergence and Retraction》; of those remaining, three chapters are brief and incomplete, insufficient to serve as method.
translations.idiomatic: The 《舊史》 (Old History) lost the chapter 《步發斂》; the three that survive are terse and incomplete—not enough to serve as a working method.

sentences.zh: 樸歷世既罕傳，予嘗問於著作佐郎劉羲候叟，羲叟為予求得其本經，然後樸之歷大備。

translations.literal: Pu's calendar through the ages has rarely been transmitted; I once inquired of Assistant in the Directorate of Authorship Liu Xi—Housou; Xisou sought for me and obtained its original classic, and only then was Pu's calendar greatly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's calendar had scarcely been handed down. I once asked Liu Xisou, Assistant in the Directorate of Authorship; he obtained the original classic for me, and only then did Pu's calendar stand complete.

sentences.zh: 羲叟好學知書史，尤通於星歷，嘗謂予曰：「前世造歷者，其法不同而多差。

translations.literal: Xisou loved learning and knew books and history, especially versed in stars and calendars; he once told me: "Former ages' calendar makers—their methods differed and mostly erred.
translations.idiomatic: Xisou was a devoted scholar of history and letters, especially expert in astronomy and calendrics. He once told me: "Calendar-makers of earlier ages used different methods, and most of them were in error.

sentences.zh: 至唐一行始以天地之中數作《大衍曆》，最為精密。

translations.literal: Reaching Tang, Yixing first used heaven-and-earth central numbers to make the 《Dayan Calendar》, most precise and close.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the Tang monk Yixing fashioned the 《大衍曆》 (Great Expansion Calendar) from the central numbers of heaven and earth did a calendar attain true precision.

sentences.zh: 後世善治歷者，皆用其法，惟寫分擬數而已。

translations.literal: Later ages' skilled calendar regulators all used his method—only copying parts and drafting numbers, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Later masters of calendrics all followed his method, merely copying fractions and adjusting figures.

translations.literal: Reaching Pu, he too could make a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, in his turn, was able to establish a school of his own.

sentences.zh: 樸之曆法，總日躔差為盈縮二歷，分月離為遲疾二百四十八限，以考衰殺之漸，以審朓朒，而朔望正矣。

translations.literal: Pu's calendar method: gather solar motion discrepancy into two calendars of surplus and wane; divide lunar departure into slow and rapid two hundred forty-eight limits, to examine decline and killing's gradations, to scrutinize waxing and waning, and new and full moons are rectified.
translations.idiomatic: In Pu's method, solar motion discrepancies are summed into paired surplus-and-wane tables; lunar motion is divided into 248 slow-and-swift limits to track diminishing and waxing, to judge the moon's phases—so that new and full moons align correctly.

sentences.zh: 校赤道九限，更其率數，以步黃道，使日躔有常度；

translations.literal: Correct the equator's nine limits, change their rate numbers, to pace the yellow path, making the sun's motion have constant degrees;
translations.idiomatic: He calibrated nine equatorial limits and revised their rates to pace the ecliptic, giving the sun's motion a fixed measure;

sentences.zh: 分黃道八節，辨其內外，以揆九道，使月行如循環，而二曜協矣。

translations.literal: Divide the yellow path's eight nodes, distinguish inner and outer, to measure the nine paths, making the moon's motion like cycling, and the two luminaries harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: he divided the ecliptic into eight nodes, distinguished inner from outer paths, and gauged the nine courses of the moon so that her motion runs in cycles and the two luminaries keep accord.

sentences.zh: 觀天勢之升降，察軌道之斜正，以制食差，而交會密矣。

translations.literal: Observe heaven's momentum's rise and fall, inspect the orbit's slant and square, to regulate eclipse discrepancy, and conjunctions grow close.
translations.idiomatic: He observed how celestial momentum rises and falls, examined whether orbits run oblique or true, and regulated eclipse discrepancy so that conjunctions grew exact.

sentences.zh: 測嶽臺之中晷，以辨二至之日夜，而軌漏實矣。

translations.literal: Measure the central gnomon at Yue Terrace, to distinguish the two solstices' day and night, and orbit clepsydra is solid.
translations.idiomatic: He measured the central gnomon at the Imperial Observatory to fix the day-lengths of the solstices, and the clepsydra matched the solar path.

sentences.zh: 推星行之逆順、伏留，使舒亟有漸，而五緯齊矣。

translations.literal: Push star motion's retrograde and direct, hiding and station, making slow and urgent have gradation, and the five luminaries align.
translations.idiomatic: He computed planets' retrograde and direct motion, their hiding and station, giving slow and swift motion proper gradation so that the five planets kept in step.

sentences.zh: 然不能宏深簡易，而徑急是取。

translations.literal: Yet he could not make it broad, deep, and simple—instead he took what was direct and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not make the system broad, deep, and simple; he took what was quick and direct.

sentences.zh: 至其所長，雖聖人出不能廢也。

translations.literal: As for what he excelled in—even if a sage appeared he could not abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: In what he did best, not even a sage could set his work aside.

sentences.zh: 」羲叟之言蓋如此，覽者得以考焉。

translations.literal: " Xisou's words were roughly thus; viewers may thereby examine.
translations.idiomatic: " Such, in sum, was Xisou's judgment, which readers may consult for themselves.
